reasoning.text: The render now passes both acceptance tests. TOP shows all eight BRAM banks, eight copper DSP multipliers as a clean column of orange dots (the prior occlusion worry is resolved — they are not mutually hidden), the two distinct reduction members, the twiddle/addr/controller cluster on the right, and the two white FIFOs. SIDE confirms the exploded butterfly lane riding correctly on its two risers above the array, and the exploded heatsink floating on its stub, with nothing sunk below or floating off the ground line. The only residual nits were dataflow legibility ones: the intra-lane multiply→add/sub→register order and the exploded datapath order lived only in the prose, the heatsink read as too few fins to be unmistakably a heatsink, and the operand-return bus had no direction marker.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank), each a DSP modular multiplier, a symmetric modular adder, a symmetric modular subtractor and a pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar to close the conflict-free read-modify-write loop. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM (feeding all multipliers), the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array, and clamp the exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder and subtractor, then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, capped with a return arrow at the crossbar end to close the conflict-free read-modify-write loop. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM (feeding all multipliers), the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
